title: NIST: standard atomic weight of Mercury (Hg, Z=80) is 200.592(3)
summary: NIST prints the standard atomic weight field of Mercury (Hg, Z=80) as 200.592(3), with the isotope rows in the same file.
body: PubChem's periodic-table row names atomic number 80, symbol Hg, as Mercury. The NIST compositions file prints the standard atomic weight of Mercury as 200.592(3). The parenthesis is the uncertainty NIST prints on the last digits of that standard atomic weight. It is an evaluated standard, not one laboratory weighing of one sample. The notes field on this element's rows is blank. Isotope rows in the same file: Hg-196 relative atomic mass 195.9658326(32), isotopic composition 0.0015(1); Hg-198 relative atomic mass 197.96676860(52), isotopic composition 0.0997(20); Hg-199 relative atomic mass 198.96828064(46), isotopic composition 0.1687(22); Hg-200 relative atomic mass 199.96832659(47), isotopic composition 0.2310(19); Hg-201 relative atomic mass 200.97030284(69), isotopic composition 0.1318(9); Hg-202 relative atomic mass 201.97064340(69), isotopic composition 0.2986(26); Hg-204 relative atomic mass 203.97349398(53), isotopic composition 0.0687(15). A relative atomic mass is scaled to carbon-12. An isotopic composition, when the field is not blank, is a representative mole fraction, not a new assay made for this card. The symbols for an interval, a parenthesis, a bracket, and a # mark are defined on world.chemistry.nist-atomic-weight-notation. This standard atomic weight is not the Chemistry WebBook molecular-weight field, which is a different catalog entry when one exists.
